envelope.author: planner
envelope.reason: Surface the handed shard intact: the failed dispatch exceeds capacity, and its existing factors do not provide a lawful smaller complete-launch partition.
envelope.cause: Main reports the second incomplete return of complete-persona-launch and requests a rectified route or the unplannable shard boundary.

payload.title: persona launch has no dispatch-sized factor cut
payload.body:
The planner surfaces the handed persona launch shard intact after the implementer's capacity finding; this is not a missing-harness prerequisite. Main reports that complete-persona-launch did not land, and agent://BuildCompletePersonaLaunch explicitly reports inability to finish the coherent unit, not an unavailable binary. Its unaccepted partial edits remain in its isolated checkout, in the canon guard source cells and committed shell targets. They are not a completed factor, accepted evidence, or an integration baseline. No checks or native activation scenarios were run.

The planner re-read the design interfaces and the bound plan at line header d8701e45. Persona launch remains version 01M3ZAHNR4MCMTZD4AKYPEA326 and factors only on enforcement scope and persona. Enforcement scope is primitive; persona is primitive and defines the individual's identity/residue, not the transport of its composed skills or the lifecycle of its executable launch. The capacity rule requires an oversized unit to split on its existing design factors before redispatch. An enforcement-scope unit can name ownership/activation work, but assigning the remaining skill delivery and executable-launch work to persona would change what that factor means. Keeping that residual as another persona-launch unit instead of a factor is not the required factor split. The planner cannot author a new conceptual factor or redraw the supplied shard.

The usage census also prevents presenting an implementation-file split as a concurrency proof: registration and complete launch both use project/index.ts, core/harness-adapter.ts, the omp and Claude renderers, and their cross-surface tests. Two simultaneous units declaring those outputs would contend. Serializing that pair produces a singleton nonterminal wave, which the current plan law rejects. Padding a wave with unchanged persona work would have acceptance already true before the unit and is equally invalid. These are planning constraints, not evidence that the design's behavioral laws should be weakened.

The original single-unit capacity judgment was the planner's defect. The later route clarification correctly established available native binaries, but it did not reduce the indivisible dispatch and did not answer this new capacity finding. No conclusion is made that enforcement scope by itself exceeds capacity; the established finding concerns the combined unit. No design amendment, retraction, or acceptance has been performed. The plan stays bound, the unlanded unit stays active but blocked by this note, and there is no ready route to hand out. The handed naming idea remains recorded against that unit pending rectification rather than being silently discarded.

The required decision belongs to the design-holder: reconsider the handed decomposition so that the required complete launch can be realized in dispatch-sized units under the existing planning laws, or supply an explicit ruling changing the relevant planning constraint. The planner will then rectify the bound plan and carry the whole existing behavioral acceptance forward. Do not redispatch the unchanged oversized unit, weaken complete skill/enforcement delivery to fit the current projection, or integrate the isolated partial edits as a finished slice.
